texts: doha on a crow-like man who chases every pretty face and loses everything
My friend ruined his marriage chasing every attractive woman he met, like a crow after scraps, and now sits alone with nothing.

Compose a doha about the crow that dives at every scrap it sees without thought, just as a man ruled by bodily craving darts after every passing temptation and ends by losing his family, honour and peace.
crow, lustful hunger
The crow dives at every scrap, and appetite drives the man; neither pauses to ask what the pursuit will cost.
Desire of the flesh blinds the seeker's eyes and drags him from the path, though he swore to walk it.
He was a sincere student of the scriptures until infatuation took hold of him, and now he cannot even remember what he once sought.
Please write a doha about how sensual craving, once it rules the mind, makes a man forget his duty, his family and his God, and leaves him with nothing but regret after the moment passes.
craving blinds the seeker
doha about how lust makes smart ppl dumb

Compose a doha showing that craving leaves a man like a handful of ash after a brief blaze, and that the scales of wisdom weigh a moment of pleasure against a lifetime of loss and always find it far lighter.
Brief is the sweetness of craving, and long the ash that follows; the scales of wisdom do not lie.
He gave up his reputation for one reckless affair, and when it ended he stood among the ashes, wondering what he'd weighed it against.
ash, scales, sensual craving
doha on lust ending in ash, the scales never lie
A saint in our region lost his reputation to a single moment of weakness for a woman, after decades of discipline, and I am still shaken by it.
Years of discipline can fall in an hour when the senses rule the mind; guard the windows of the eyes.
doha on resisting temptation, even a saint can fall
Compose a doha about how a seeker who has spent decades in restraint can be undone in a moment by bodily craving, and why the wise keep a constant watch over their senses until their last breath.
guard the senses
conquer your urges
The urge that rises in the blood is a tyrant; the wise man refuses it his throne.
Please write a doha about how the one who masters bodily craving is a true conqueror, greater than kings who win wars, because he has defeated the enemy that lives within him and rules all men.
doha on control over physical desires
I decided to give up a long and unhealthy attachment to a woman who was not good for me, and it felt like winning a war within myself.
Craving and love are far apart; one devours, the other offers all, and only the second walks to God.
craving is not love

Compose a doha about the difference between true love, which gives itself to the beloved, and sensual craving, which only takes for itself, so that the seeker may know which of the two leads him toward the divine.
After my breakup I realized what I had called love was just craving, because when it faded I found nothing of her in my heart.
doha on difference between love and lust

Compose a doha about the lion that rules the wilds and fears nothing but is brought down by a single moment of bodily craving, showing that no strength, rank or courage can protect a man from his own senses.
The lion who conquers kingdoms is chained by craving; the senses are the strongest hunter of all.
lion, craving's trap
doha on strong men falling to lust
My uncle, a lion of a man at work, was brought down by an affair that cost him his job, his family and his name.
Please write a doha about how craving binds a person with fine threads he does not feel until he is caught, and how the churn of the mind brings out butter only when he is free of them.
Craving binds with threads you cannot feel; only the churn of wisdom can loosen them.
thread, churn, craving
doha on lust is a thread that traps u slowly, churn the mind
It started with little glances and messages, a thread of attraction I did not notice, until my whole life was tangled in it.
The potter shapes the clay; but craving shapes the weak man, and he is broken in its grip.
doha on potter and clay: lust breaks you like a pot
A potter I knew, a good man, was undone by a wandering eye and left his workshop and his family.
Please write a doha about the potter who moulds clay into a vessel but loses his own form when he yields to bodily craving, which breaks the finest vessels of character into useless pieces.
potter, clay, craving

Please write a doha explaining that sensual craving may feel like a feast but is a famine in disguise, because the more it is fed the hungrier it grows, and the seeker who gives in never reaches his goal.
craving never satisfied
doha on how giving in to lust only makes it stronger
I told myself just once, and then again, and now I can't stop; I am looking for a verse to help me break this cycle.
The more it is fed, the hungrier it grows; the wise starve it and are free.
furnace, craving, restraint
He worked at the blacksmith's furnace all day to wear out his urges, and the old smith told him that restraint is better than exhaustion.
doha on furnace of lust, how to cool down
Write a doha about the furnace of bodily craving that blazes in youth and consumes those who feed it, and about how the wise learn early to control it by discipline, prayer and good company.
The furnace of craving roars in the young; wise is he who learns to bank it before it takes him.
The thief of the senses steals the seeker's wisdom while he sleeps, and wakes him poor.
doha on lust as a thief that steals ur peace
I was so close to finishing my studies when infatuation robbed me of my focus, like a thief in the night, and I lost an entire year.
thief, craving

Please write a doha about how sensual craving is a thief that steals wisdom, health, reputation and the peace of a household while a man thinks he is only enjoying himself, and how only vigilance protects him.
Write a doha about the moon-faced beauty who seems as pure as a lotus and the seeker who is lured by her looks to forget his purpose, teaching him to look beyond the bodily form to the soul within.
The moon is lovely and the lotus lovelier still, but wise is he who admires without craving.
I was drawn to a woman with a face like the moon and eyes like lotus petals, and it took months to see that I was in love with an appearance.
moon, lotus, bodily craving
doha on moon-faced beauty and lotus eyes, craving appearance
After years of marriage, I caught myself ogling women half my age, and I was disgusted with myself, and I want a verse to help me restore my self-respect.
restrain wandering eyes
doha on controlling your eyes and mind
The roving glance leads the heart astray; turn it inward and find the peace you seek.
Please write a doha about the way a man who lets his eyes follow every passing face loses his mind, his focus and finally his dignity, and about how self-restraint is the only road to peace.
beggar, craving
The beggar of the senses never fills his bowl; however much he gets, he begs for more.
The more he indulged his appetites, the more he wanted, like a beggar who knows no limit, until nothing satisfied him at all.
doha on lust as a beggar always asking for more

Compose a doha about the way bodily craving is a beggar that is never satisfied, always asking for more, however much it receives, and about how the wise refuse to be its servants and live in freedom.

Write a doha about the seeker who sits at night beneath the moon and fights the pull of bodily craving, showing that the seeker's struggle is greater than any worldly battle and that victory is worth a lifetime of practice.
On a moonlit night, I paced my room for hours battling a strong craving for my ex, and by dawn I had won, and I felt like a conqueror.
moon, battling craving
Beneath the moon the seeker fights the war within; blessed is the one who prevails.
doha on resisting lust at night under the moon
craving drags you down

Compose a doha showing that sensual craving drags the seeker down from the heights he has climbed through years of devotion, and that only constant remembrance of God and keeping good company can protect him from the fall.
The senses drag the climber down; grip the Name tightly, and the peak is yours.
doha about how lust pulls people off the spiritual path
My friend, after ten years of meditation, nearly threw everything away for an infatuation, and it took his teacher to call him back.
I keep going back to someone who I know is bad for me, even though I promised myself a hundred times that I would stop, and I need strength.
doha on breaking a toxic attraction
Though the eyes are drawn and the body yearns, the awakened mind says no, and stays free.
say no to temptation
Please write a doha about how a seeker must say no to the pull of bodily temptation again and again until the habit of restraint becomes his nature and the peace that follows becomes his reward.
doha on how lust distracts from everything important
Compose a doha showing that a mind full of sensual thoughts has no room for prayer, study or honest work, and that the seeker who wants to progress must first quiet this restless hunger of the body.
distracted by desire
When the body's hunger fills the mind, prayer finds no place to stay.
I used to be the top student in my class, but after I fell for a classmate I could not focus on a single page for weeks.
The king in his palace had every comfort and a hundred wives, yet no peace, while the wandering swan in our pond had only reeds and seemed far more content.
In the palace of pleasure the king is a prisoner; the swan floats free, wanting nothing.
palace, swan, craving
Compose a doha about the king who lived among all the pleasures of his palace and yet was never satisfied, and the swan that glides free of every craving, showing which of the two is truly rich.
doha on swan vs palace life, sensual pleasure never satisfies
ruined by desire
doha about a man who destroyed his life over a woman
He was a respected man until a sudden obsession consumed him, and within a year he lost his job, his wife and his good name.
One reckless hour of craving can undo a lifetime of honour, and no repentance restores it.
Write a doha showing that the man who loses control of his bodily appetites loses everything he built, and that the shame which follows lasts far longer than the brief pleasure that caused it.
fire, hungry body
The fire in my blood kept me up all night, and I wanted a verse that could help me put it out without giving in.

Write a doha about the fire of bodily craving that blinds the seeker and drags him from the path, and how only the cool water of discipline and remembrance can quench it before it consumes his whole life.
doha on the fire of lust, how to put it out
The fire of the senses consumes the one who feeds it; cool it with restraint, and live.

Please write a doha about the way sensual indulgence weakens the body, dulls the mind and drives away peace, and how the seeker who guards his energy through restraint gains clarity, strength and a joy that lasts.
Preserve your strength, O seeker; scatter it not on the passing urge, for it is the source of vision.
doha on conserving energy by controlling desires
restraint gives strength
After I stopped chasing every attraction and focused on my work, my health and my concentration improved so much that my friends noticed.

Write a doha about the man who wears the sacred mark on his forehead and chants loudly but whose eyes follow every woman who passes, showing that outward religion without inner restraint is a deception.
The mark on the brow is bright, but the eyes below it wander; what use is the sign if the mind is not still?
doha on a tilak wearing hypocrite with wandering eyes
tilak, wandering eyes
The man who leads our evening prayers wears a big mark on his forehead yet leers at every young woman, and I am disgusted.
I stood by the well hoping to see a girl who drew water there each morning, and I realised I had come not to draw water but to feed an urge.
Compose a doha about a youth who goes daily to the well not for water but to watch a passing girl, and about how his craving wastes his hours and leaves his own thirst for truth unquenched.
He came to the well for water, but his thirst was of another kind, and it was never slaked.
doha on a guy who hangs around the well just to see a girl
well, wasted desire
doha on river and thread: lust pulls you along like a current
river, thread, craving
I got swept along like a river by an infatuation that tied my life up in a thread of lies, and now I am trying to find my way back.
Compose a doha showing that bodily craving is a river that sweeps away everything in its path, and a fine thread of lies that ties the man who is carried by it until he cannot move.
The river of craving carries the weak, and the thread of deceit binds them as they drift.
doha on a grindstone crushing a man who gave in to lust
grindstone, desire
My neighbour's affair ground his family down like a grindstone and left all of them broken.
Please write a doha about how bodily craving is like a grindstone that grinds the lives of the family, the reputation of the man and the peace of his family into dust, leaving only bitterness behind.
The grindstone of craving crushes the grain of years; what was nourishing becomes dust.
After a night of indulgence I woke to a barren feeling like sand, and I wondered how I could ever fill that emptiness by repeating the same thing.
doha on lust leaves u empty like sand
Craving is a mirage on the sand; the thirsty run to it and find only dust.
sand, empty craving
Write a doha about how the pleasures of the flesh slip through the fingers like sand, leaving emptiness and regret, and how only lasting devotion can give a satisfaction that does not run away.
gold, craving, ruin
Gold and craving are twin masters; the one who serves them both is a slave in a heavy chain.
Compose a doha about the man who gives his gold to feed his bodily cravings and finds himself poor in honour and wealth, showing that what is spent on the senses is lost forever without return.
doha on wasting gold on sensual pleasure
My cousin spent all the gold he had inherited on a life of indulgence and now has neither a friend nor a coin to his name.
A friend of mine says sensual enjoyment is life's purpose, but I see how restless and empty he looks, and I would like a verse to answer him.
doha on why chasing pleasure doesnt make u happy
Seek not joy in the senses; they promise much, and leave the seeker poorer than he began.
Please write a doha about the false promise of sensual pleasure, which appears to offer happiness but leaves the seeker emptier, and the lasting peace that comes only from mastering the urges.
pleasures that deceive
The senses run wild if untrained; the wise man holds them firm, the foolish one is dragged.
My brother never learnt to say no to his appetites, and now at forty he is exhausted, in debt and ashamed.
master your senses

Compose a doha about the five senses that run wild when not trained, dragging the unwary toward ruin, and about how the seeker must take firm hold of them through discipline and the company of the wise.
doha on controlling the five senses
Write a doha showing that anyone who allows the craving of the body to rule him cannot see truth, because desire dims judgment, and only the cool mind of a restrained seeker perceives clearly.
desire blinds
When I was infatuated I believed every lie she told me, and only when it ended did I see how blind I had been.
Where the body's hunger rules, the eyes of wisdom are closed; restraint alone gives sight.
doha on how lust makes you blind to the truth
doha on the shroud and lust, in the end it all means nothing
Write a doha about the shroud that awaits every body, the same body we spend so much of our lives indulging and decorating, to remind the seeker of how little the pleasures of the flesh are worth.
The body you adorn is soon to wear a shroud; why then squander your days on its cravings?
At my uncle's funeral, seeing the white shroud, I suddenly felt silly about all the years I had spent running after bodily pleasures.
shroud, bodily cravings
swan, pure mind
doha on swan staying pure while others fall to lust
The swan glides on muddy water yet remains spotless; so the wise live among temptations untouched.
My friend works in an environment full of temptation and yet stays clean, like a swan on muddy water, and I hope to be like him.
Compose a doha about the swan that moves among the mud of the world and remains white, showing that the seeker too can live among temptations without losing his purity if he keeps his mind watchful.
Even the strong are made weak by the hunger of the senses; mightier is the mind that does not bow.
doha on will power against urges
I have been sober and disciplined for two years, and last night an old temptation returned, but I managed to resist it with one deep breath.
resist the urge
Compose a doha showing that the seeker's real battle is not against outer enemies but against the urges of his own body, and that each time he refuses them, he becomes stronger and freer.
The physician can heal the fever of the body, yet who heals the fever of craving? Only the Name, and the patience of years.

Please write a doha about the physician who cures every bodily illness but cannot cure the disease of sensual craving, which only the seeker can heal through discipline, devotion and a wise teacher, more precious than gold.
doha on physician and gold can't cure lust, only discipline
physician, gold, restraint
My physician friend can heal almost anything for gold, but he confessed that he could not cure his own habit of chasing women.
shadow, blind man, desire
I followed the shadow of an attraction for a year like a blind man, and only when it vanished did I understand how little was there.

Compose a doha about the blind man who follows the shadow of bodily craving in the belief that it is a guide, and falls into ruin, whereas the seeker of truth turns from the shadow and finds the real light.
Craving is a shadow that leads the blind; he follows it into the pit and calls it love.
doha on chasing a shadow like a blind man, lust makes you blind
At the mosque the faithful bow, but the blind man's eyes see more clearly than the lustful who stand beside him.
doha on a blind man seeing truth better than a lustful man in the mosque
At the mosque I saw a blind man praying with such purity of mind, while the young man beside him could not stop glancing at the women.
mosque, blind man, wandering eyes
Compose a doha showing that a blind man who prays at the mosque with a clean mind sees more of God than the sighted man whose eyes and thoughts wander toward the women around him.

Write a doha about how the cravings of the body bring momentary pleasure and lasting grief, and the seeker who sees this clearly gives them up without regret and finds a calm happiness no indulgence ever gave.
doha on short pleasure vs long pain
brief pleasure, long grief
Every time I gave in, I felt great for ten minutes and awful for ten days, and finally I understood the bargain I was making.
A moment's joy, a lifetime's tears; wise is he who sees the price before he pays.
When desire rules the mind, the soul is a stranger in its own body; turn within, and be whole again.
doha on coming back to yourself after temptation
After months of being lost in an obsession, I feel like a stranger to myself, and want to find my way back to calm.
return to yourself

Please write a doha about the seeker who has strayed into sensual temptation and then returns to himself in repentance, and how the Lord receives him back without reproach and sets him on the path once more.
My teacher says that the body's cravings are the first and last enemy of a spiritual life, and I wish to understand why through a verse.
doha on why cravings are the enemy of spiritual life
Compose a doha about how the cravings of the body, left unchecked, are the first enemy a seeker meets and the last he conquers, and how patience, practice and the grace of the guru help him to win.
the seeker's enemy
The first foe and the last is in your own flesh; conquer it and no other enemy remains.
The rose of pleasure hides a thorn that pierces the unwary; do not reach for what will make you bleed.
thorn, temptation
doha on thorns in the rose of pleasure
Write a doha about the rose of sensual pleasure that attracts with its beauty but hides a thorn, and about how the wise look first for the thorn before reaching out and so remain safe and calm.
I was attracted to a coworker who seemed perfect, but the thorn of her manipulation soon showed itself, and I'm glad I stepped back in time.
Compose a doha about the sorrow of a man who gives his days to sensual pursuits and wakes in old age to find his strength, his friends and his chances gone, and nothing left of his life.
My old uncle looks back on a youth spent chasing pleasures and says he has nothing to show for it, not even a memory worth keeping.
doha on how chasing pleasure in youth leaves old age empty
wasted youth
Youth spent on appetite leaves old age with nothing; spend your strength on what lasts.
The lion roars in the wilderness of the senses, yet the single string of the lute silences him with a note of the Name.
Please write a doha about the lion of bodily craving that roars in the mind, and the single note of the one-string lute, the remembrance of God, which alone can quiet it and bring the seeker peace.
My lion of an urge woke every night until I picked up my one-string lute and sang the Name, and slowly it fell silent.
lion, one-string lute, calm
doha on lion of lust tamed by a lute and singing God's name
The tree of pleasure bears fruit that turns to dust; churn the cream of wisdom instead, and take its butter.
Compose a doha about how the tree of sensual pleasure bears sweet-looking fruit that is bitter within, while the churn of discipline and meditation turns the cream of life into the butter of peace.
tree, churn, restraint
My grandfather sat under the tree each evening, churning buttermilk, and told me that restraint is the only thing that makes any pleasure last.
doha on the tree of pleasure and churn of wisdom
doha on staying faithful to your partner when tempted
stay faithful
A colleague has been making advances toward me although I am married, and I want a verse to remind me why I must stay true.

Please write a doha about the honour of a person who stays faithful to his marriage vows in the face of temptation, and about how that loyalty brings a peace and trust that no brief pleasure can ever match.
Faithful is the one who turns from the passing temptation; his loyalty is a lasting joy.
doha on salt and crossroads: temptations at every turn, stay on track

Write a doha about the traveller who stands at the crossroads where the paths of pleasure and of discipline part, tasting the salt of bodily temptation and learning that it only makes him thirstier for more.
Standing at a crossroads in my life, I realised that chasing pleasures only left a salty taste of regret, and I chose the harder path.
At the crossroads one road is sweet and ends in salt; the other is hard and ends in peace.
salt, crossroads, temptation
pearl, restraint
My grandmother kept a single pearl all her life as a symbol of her discipline, saying that a restrained life forms its own pearl.
The pearl forms slowly in the oyster of restraint; scatter it on the senses and it is gone.
doha on pearl and self-control, treasure not wasted

Compose a doha about the pearl of a seeker's life, which is formed over long years of discipline and which he must not throw away on a moment's craving, since once lost it cannot easily be found again.
doha on a moneylender who gambled everything on pleasure

Please write a doha about the moneylender whose wealth and reputation were destroyed by his craving for sensual pleasures, showing that no amount of money can buy back self-respect once it is squandered on the senses.
moneylender, ruined by desire
He counted other men's coins, yet could not count the cost of his own desires; the account came due.
The moneylender in our town, once so respected, spent everything he had on indulgences and now begs from the people he used to lend to.
Under the stars last night I decided to stop chasing every passing attraction, and the sky seemed to nod in approval.
doha on stars and calm after giving up lust
Write a doha about how the stars shine above every human weakness in perfect stillness, teaching the seeker that when he rises above the urges of the body, he too becomes calm, clear and radiant.
stars, peace of restraint
The stars shine calm above the restless world; so shines the soul that has conquered its craving.
